wins.text: Federal Express adjusted operating income grew $146M YoY on essentially flat revenue, with adjusted operating profit up 13% YoY, demonstrating strong cost transformation progress
DRIVE savings of $540M in Q2, on track to deliver $2.2B in incremental savings for FY'25 and $4B total by end of FY'25 vs. FY'23 baseline
International export package volumes increased 9% YoY; International Priority freight average daily pounds up 10% and international economy freight up 5%, signaling early Tricolor strategy progress
Completed $1B in share repurchases in Q2, bringing YTD total to $2B with an additional $500M planned for H2 FY'25

Nonstandard surcharges generating over $180M annualized YoY benefit from new AI image capture process; dimensional pricing at Charles de Gaulle hub expected to deliver $50M+ operating income benefit in FY'25

risks.text: FY'25 adjusted diluted EPS guidance cut to $19–$20 from prior $20–$21, driven by weaker-than-expected industrial economy and revenue shortfall; revenue net-of-cost headwind widened to $700M from prior $100M estimate
FedEx Freight operating profit down $179M YoY in Q2; average daily shipments down 8% and weight per shipment down 3% due to soft industrial economy; revenue expected to decline slightly in H2 FY'25
U.S. Postal Service contract expiration creating ~$500M full-year operating profit headwind, with Q3 impact expected to be the largest before easing in Q4
U.S. manufacturing PMI in contraction for 24 of the past 25 months — the second longest downturn in U.S. history — suppressing B2B volumes which represent ~60% of FEC revenue and ~90% of LTL revenue
Competitive pricing environment pressuring base rates and yields in both parcel and LTL; international export yield pressure estimated at $300M headwind for FY'25

guidance_items.detail: FY'25 adjusted diluted EPS revised to $19–$20 from prior $20–$21; midpoint implies ~9.6% YoY adjusted EPS growth on approximately flat revenue
Top end assumes low single-digit revenue growth; low end assumes low single-digit revenue decline; midpoint assumes roughly flat revenue YoY vs. prior assumption of modest growth
Continue to expect YoY adjusted operating margin expansion at Federal Express and margin contraction at FedEx Freight for full year FY'25
Full-year DRIVE savings target of $2.2B incremental savings reaffirmed, with sequential build expected in Q3 and Q4

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Potential USPS privatization and its impact on the competitive landscape
Tariff pull-forward demand and network agility under a new trade policy regime
Customer attrition risk and bundle strategy implications from the FedEx Freight separation
